title: Rebuild when the premise is rejected
statement: When review rejects a draft's premise, rebuild on the corrected premise instead of polishing the same design, and never revive a rejected concept because its code exists.
detail: Early drafts of a Grade 9 unit opening were rejected as too childish, too like a guide-led dashboard, or too like an app showing images rather than a storytelling experience; the 6 October handover records that criticism as a design correction, not a request for more decorative polish on the same premise, and says not to resurrect those concepts simply because code exists (line 62). It names another visually polished deliverable that solves the wrong problem as the largest creative risk (line 483).
against: The same handover sets a limit: open choices are to be decided with real evidence when they matter, and they are not a reason to discard existing work or reopen settled creative decisions (line 489). A guide character rejected in the early drafts came back on 7 October as the film's narrator because a brief called for it, not because its code existed (`g9/film/v07/README.md`, line 11).
